editorial.titleTr: Party Chief Ignites Shincheonji Probe; Ruling Party Must Follow Through with Accountability
summaryTr: Party conflict intensifies over disclosure of investigation results into allegations of Shincheonji cult group mass recruitment
Allegations raised in 2022 reignite ahead of 2026 party convention
Given that collusion between politics and religion is a serious crime, disclosure of results and referral for investigation are necessary
editorial.bodyTr: Conflict within the Democratic Party has intensified over whether to disclose investigation results regarding suspicions of collective entry by Shincheonji members into the party. The allegation was raised during the 2022 presidential primary election but subsequently died down, only to reignite with recent remarks ahead of the 2026 party convention. Since collusion between religion and politics constitutes a serious crime, the party must clearly reveal its investigation findings and take responsible measures such as referring the matter to prosecution.

summaryTr: Individual hacker using AI hacks into enterprise-level server, steals 8.2 million pieces of information.
Police arrest 7 extortionists, but security threats continue to escalate.
Government and businesses urgently need to strengthen security investment and investigation response.
editorials.bodyTr: For the first time, a large-scale personal information theft has been confirmed in which an ordinary person using AI breached servers at the level of major corporations. Police arrested seven individuals who extracted 8.2 million pieces of personal information from 90 locations and then used it for extortion. As hacking becomes faster and easier, security investments and investigative responses are lagging behind, necessitating stronger countermeasures.

summaryTr: Seoul's Seocho District plans to impose reconstruction environmental charges on Banpo redevelopment apartments by year-end

The government must preempt controversy by improving the standard
editorials.bodyTr: Seoul's Seocho District has announced it will levy a reassessment profit-sharing charge on apartment units in the Banpo redevelopment project by year's end. The reassessment profit-sharing system is designed to collect a portion of excess profits from the state and local governments when profits per member exceed 80 million won. Since the calculation standards fail to adequately reflect differences in inflation and timing of land acquisition, the government should refine these criteria to prevent further controversy.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Intimidating the Chief Justice—Is Presidential Pardon Really the Top Priority?
summaryTr: The Democratic Party of Korea has officially announced plans to pursue a state investigation into Chief Justice Jo Hee-dae and a special prosecution law regarding fabricated indictments.
The ruling party is undermining the separation of powers by intimidating the head of the judiciary over dissatisfaction with court rulings it desired.
If the party continues to focus solely on 'judicial protection' while turning a blind eye to livelihood measures, public discontent will only grow further.
editorial.bodyTr: The Democratic Party has formalized its push for a National Assembly investigation into Chief Justice Jo Hee-dae and special prosecution legislation regarding fabricated charges. Democratic Party Senior Spokesperson Park Sung-jun said yesterday that "the investigation into Chief Justice Jo and the special prosecution act on fabricated charges are very significant tasks the Democratic Party must pursue after the parliamentary audit." The party's leadership has already reviewed detailed procedures for this. It appears the party is dusting off the impeachment card against the chief justice, which some party members have been stirring up using the appellate court's acquittal in the controversy over Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon's alleged conspiracy to conduct and pay for opinion polls. Riding on this momentum, the ruling party also intends to push forward with special prosecution legislation regarding the fabricated charges in President Lee Jae-myung's indictment cases. There is cause for concern when the ruling party invokes the specter of a "judicial cartel," blames the chief justice for failing to deliver the verdicts it desires, and threatens to forcibly remove him. Using legislative supermajority power to intimidate the head of the judiciary seriously undermines the constitutional principles of separation of powers and judicial independence. The Democratic Party is proceeding to forcibly enact the special prosecution act under the guise of judicial and prosecutorial reform. Reports indicate that Representatives Park Gyun-taek and Yang Bu-nam, both from the "Presidential Case Dismissal of Charges Group," are being seriously considered as candidates for the vacant Justice Ministry post for the past two months. The prospect of appointing these figures, who are known as typical "judicial bodyguards" for taking the lead in addressing the president's judicial risks in cases like Daejang-dong, as heads of law-abiding administration naturally raises doubts about the fairness and political neutrality of investigations. While some surveys show signs of a rebound, presidential approval ratings remain at the bottom. The Democratic Party's approval ratings also continue to decline as they fall behind the People Power Party. As real estate policy failures, ranked first in negative assessments of state affairs, go uncorrected, homeless individuals pushed into a jeonse and monthly rent crisis face deepening hardship, while small business owners and self-employed workers hit hard by high prices and high interest rates endure mounting pain. The people, whose lives are difficult, want substantive livelihood measures and a shift away from failed policy directions. Yet the ruling forces seem to be going all-in with "judicial immunity" through chief justice impeachment and presidential charge dismissal as their top priority in state affairs, while turning a deaf ear to the people's suffering. If the ruling bloc continues to set aside the task of addressing the people's lives and instead focuses solely on resolving judicial risks, a further erosion of public support will be inevitable.

editorial.title: NK's closer alliance
editorial.body: Pyongyang, Beijing, Moscow draw closer; Seoul, Washington cannot afford division North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s visit to Dandong, China, on Saturday was ostensibly meant to underscore the two countries’ “blood alliance,” but its underlying aim appears to be expanding economic cooperation with China. More than 70 percent of bilateral trade passes through the border city. If expanded cross-border trade gives North Korea greater economic breathing room, efforts to pressure Pyongyang into denuclearization are likely to lose their effectiveness. Sanctions have been virtually the only tool available to pressure North Korea to denuclearize. Until just a few years ago, China and Russia cooperated with international sanctions despite the risk of straining their relations with Pyongyang. But if China, which accounts for 90 percent of North Korea’s foreign trade, appears willing to give Pyongyang greater latitude to evade sanctions, resolving the North Korean nuclear issue will become even more difficult. North Korea is already openly flouting sanctions while acquiring advanced military technologies from Russia. Eleven UN member states, including South Korea, the United States and Japan, have established the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team to monitor the implementation of sanctions against North Korea. The monitoring mechanism must be strengthened, and diplomatic pressure on China and Russia stepped up. Achieving these goals requires not only a strong South Korea-US alliance, but also close coordination with Japan. A US-China summit is scheduled for Nov. 18-19 on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen, China. Speculation has periodically surfaced that the meeting could pave the way for talks between Washington and Pyongyang before or after the summit. However, the prevailing view is that a possible meeting with US President Donald Trump was not discussed during Kim’s visit to Dandong. If US-North Korea talks do take place, South Korea must ensure that it is not sidelined in discussions of the North’s nuclear program and other security issues on the Korean Peninsula. Above all, effective communication between Seoul and Washington is essential to ensure that South Korea’s position is adequately reflected in any negotiations. 김정은 북한 지도자가 토요일 중국 단둥을 방문한 것은 겉으로는 두 나라의 '혈맹' 관계를 강조하려는 의도로 보이지만, 실제 목적은 중국과의 경제협력 확대에 있는 것으로 보인다. 양국 교역의 70% 이상이 이 국경 도시를 통과한다. 확대된 국경 간 무역이 북한에 더 큰 경제적 숨통을 열어준다면, 평양을 비핵화로 유도하려는 압박 노력의 효과는 크게 떨어질 것이다.

지금까지 제재가 북한을 비핵화로 압박할 수 있는 거의 유일한 수단이었다. 불과 몇 년 전까지만 해도 중국과 러시아는 평양과의 관계를 악화시킬 위험을 감수하면서도 국제 제재에 협력했다. 하지만 북한 외교 교역량의 90%를 차지하는 중국이 평양의 제재 회피에 더 많은 여지를 줄 의사가 있어 보인다면, 북한 핵 문제 해결은 훨씬 더 어려워질 것이다. 북한은 이미 제재를 공공연히 무시하면서 러시아로부터 첨단 군사 기술을 획득하고 있다.

남한, 미국, 일본을 포함한 11개 유엔 회원국은 북한에 대한 제재 이행을 감시하기 위한 다자간 제재 모니터링팀을 구성했다. 모니터링 메커니즘을 강화하고 중국과 러시아에 대한 외교적 압박을 강화해야 한다. 이러한 목표를 달성하려면 강력한 한미 동맹뿐만 아니라 일본과의 긴밀한 조율이 필요하다.

미중 정상회담이 11월 18~19일 중국 선전에서 개최되는 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의 계기에 예정되어 있다. 이 회담이 정상회담 전후 미북 대화의 길을 열 수 있다는 관측이 주기적으로 제기되어 왔다. 하지만 일반적인 전망은 김정은의 단둥 방문 중에 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령과의 만남 가능성이 논의되지 않았다는 것이다.

미북 대화가 실제로 진행된다면, 한국은 북한의 핵 문제 및 한반도 안보 문제에 대한 협상에서 배제되지 않도록 해야 한다. 무엇보다 서울과 워싱턴 간의 효과적인 소통이 필수적이어서 한국의 입장이 모든 협상에 적절히 반영되도록 해야 한다. 두 동맹국은 또한 평양과의 거래에 명확한 원칙을 세우고 북한이 의미 있는 약속 없이 제재 해제 같은 양보를 얻지 못하도록 더욱 긴밀히 협력해야 한다.

지난달 두만강을 가로질러 북한과 러시아를 연결하는 도로 다리가 개통되어, 평양의 북부 두 이웃 국가와의 운송 연결이 더욱 확대되었다. 이러한 연결을 통해 북한은 러시아로부터 군사적 이점을 얻으면서 동시에 중국과의 경제 관계를 확대할 것으로 예상된다. 북한, 중국, 러시아의 정렬이 심화되는 것은 우려할 만한 일이다.

우크라이나 전쟁에서 러시아를 위해 군대를 파병한 대가로 북한은 첨단 군사 기술에 접근하게 되었고, 드론, 전자전, 정밀 타격을 포함하는 현대적 전쟁 경험을 축적했다. 이는 실전 경험이 제한적인 한국 군에 심각한 위협이 된다.

평양, 베이징, 모스크바가 결집하는 가운데 서울과 워싱턴 간의 긴밀한 조율이 그 어느 때보다 필수적이다. 이를 위해 두 동맹국은 소통의 긴장을 해소하고 상호 신뢰를 재구축하기 위해 신속하게 행동해야 한다. 한국이 동맹국과의 신뢰 회복에 진지한 노력을 기울이지 않으면서 독자적인 외교 정책을 추구하려고 고집한다면, 워싱턴과 평양 양쪽 모두에서 배제될 위험에 처하게 될 것이다.

평양, 베이징, 모스크바가 결집하는 가운데 서울과 워싱턴 간의 긴밀한 조율이 그 어느 때보다 필수적이다. 이를 위해 두 동맹국은 소통의 긴장을 해소하고 상호 신뢰를 재구축하기 위해 신속하게 행동해야 한다. 한국이 동맹국과의 신뢰 회복에 진지한 노력을 기울이지 않으면서 독자적인 외교 정책을 추구하려고 고집한다면, 워싱턴과 평양 양쪽 모두에서 배제될 위험에 처하게 될 것이다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Bank of Korea Warns Youth Face Steeper Barriers to Permanent Employment
summaryTr: The Bank of Korea has diagnosed that it is becoming increasingly difficult for young people to enter regular employment.
Youth unemployment and non-regular employment issues are intensifying due to structural changes in the labor market.
This is a time when active measures from the government and businesses are needed.
